## Expression on this line

Computational at Order 7 is **systematic computational design**: the deliberate
construction of computational systems based on explicit principles. "I design this
algorithm because I have reasoned about it" — computational design is self-authored
rather than inherited. The computer scientist who designs an algorithm, the mathematician
who constructs a proof, the engineer who builds a system — these are Stage 9
computational architects.

The key advance from Stage 8 is **systemic computational modeling**. The agent does not
just see multiple perspectives on computation — it sees how computational methods interact
as a dynamic system with feedback loops, emergent properties, and structural constraints.

Computation at Stage 9 is understood as **designable**. The agent believes that
computation can be intentionally improved through rational analysis and systematic design.
This is the modernist computation: algorithms are engineering problems that can be solved
with the right design.

But computational reasoning at Stage 9 is still **framework-bound**. The agent designs
computational systems within a particular framework (imperative, functional, object-
oriented) but cannot step outside the framework to evaluate it.

The transition from Stage 9 to Stage 10 occurs when the agent can evaluate entire
computational frameworks.

In human development, Stage 9 corresponds to the professional who can construct and
defend a systematic computational theory.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Institutional computational design culture emerges. Universities, software
  companies, algorithmic research institutes.

- **UR:** The individual agent can construct and evaluate computational systems using
  explicit principles.

- **LL:** Systemic computational institutions emerge: programming languages, software
  engineering methodologies, computational research centers.

- **LR:** The university, the software company, the algorithmic research institute.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Methodological hubris — the belief that one's computational
  approach is objectively true and all others are wrong.

- **Dark allergy:** Anti-computational nihilism — the rejection of all systematic
  computational reasoning.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to systematic computational reasoning as the only
  valid approach.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting systematic computation as dehumanizing.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Systemic computational modeling:** The agent can trace computational dynamics and
  predict how changes affect system behavior.

- **Design-based computational reasoning:** The agent proposes computational
  improvements based on analysis.

- **Framework-bound analysis:** The agent reasons brilliantly within a computational
  framework but cannot evaluate the framework itself.

- **Expert-dependent design:** Computational design is concentrated in professionals.
